title: Count Nodes in a Left-Packed Tree
statement:
You get the root of a complete binary tree: every level is full except possibly the last, and the last level's nodes are packed to the left with no gaps. Return the number of nodes.

Counting every node works, but try to do better than O(n) by using the shape.

examples.why: Two full levels (3 nodes) plus two nodes on the last level, packed to the left.
An empty tree has no nodes.
Three full levels: 2³ − 1. Equal values do not matter; only the shape does.

hints: Walking down the leftmost edge gives the height. Walking down the rightmost edge gives another height. What does it mean when they are equal?
If the left and right edge heights of a subtree are equal, that subtree is perfect and has 2^h − 1 nodes, with no need to look inside.
Otherwise count 1 + count(left) + count(right). In a complete tree at most one child at each level is not perfect, so the recursion follows one path: O(log² n).

explain.intuition:
A perfect tree of height h has exactly 2^h − 1 nodes. In a complete tree you can tell whether a subtree is perfect cheaply: walk its leftmost edge and its rightmost edge. If both have the same length, the last level is full and you know the count without visiting the inside.

If they differ, split at the root. Because the last level is packed to the left, at least one of the two children is perfect, so it returns after one edge walk. Only one branch goes deeper. There are O(log n) levels, and each one costs an O(log n) edge walk, so the total is O(log² n) instead of O(n).
steps: Count lh, the steps down the left edge, and rh, the steps down the right edge, both starting at node.
pitfalls: Comparing the heights of the left and right subtrees by their left edges only. That says which side holds the last node, not whether the current subtree is perfect.
Off by one in the power: a perfect tree with h levels has 2^h − 1 nodes, not 2^h.
Thinking the shortcut also works on any tree. It relies on the last level being packed left.

solutions.title: Count every node
solutions.idea: Plain recursion: 1 for the node plus the counts of both subtrees. Ignores the shape.

solutions.title: Skip perfect subtrees
solutions.idea: If the leftmost and rightmost paths have the same length, the subtree is perfect and its size is 2^h − 1. Otherwise recurse; only one side can be imperfect.
